title: Module Controlled Functions: Component Locations
introduction:
I use this drawing as a seating chart for the Mustang's body electronics. The cyan component portraits show what to look for; their leader lines end at the corresponding locations in the transparent vehicle. Match a portrait's circled callout to the table's Item column, then read its Description. Follow the line all the way to its endpoint—the portrait's position around the page is just room for the drawing.

DDM means driver door module, PDM means passenger door module, and RTM means radio transceiver module. The door-module leaders identify their respective doors. For the RTM, choose the table entry matching Convertible or Coupe before following its leader; these are body-style alternatives. Keep BCM and Body Control Module B (BCM-B) distinct rather than treating their similar names as interchangeable.

The BCM coordinates body electrical functions and exchanges information with other controllers. That makes this map useful for finding the right participant in a system, but a module's address is not a guilty verdict. The illustration and table establish identity and general location; they do not provide trim-removal access, connector pinouts, electrical tests or replacement instructions.
